extracted.intended_audience: local news editors, journalists, newsroom leaders, funders and community partners in the American South interested in adopting constructive journalism practices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for adopting constructive journalism practices in local/regional newsrooms, including the movement's definition, ethical commitments, core pillars (solutions, nuance, conversation), and measurable outcomes to evaluate impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Constructive journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journalism is a global movement that questions journalists’ understanding of their role as passive observer, prompting a fresh look at the relationship between media outlets and the communities they cover. Constructive journalism acknowledges that the stories the media covers and how they cover them both reflect and shape the narrative of their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach looks forward, seeking out and elevating information that can help people to make progress together. It adds an additional layer of awareness about how people are impacted by reporting and stresses that journalism should be both critical and constructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three Pillars of Constructive Journalism (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Three Pillars framework (adapted from the Constructive Institute) combines multiple dimensions—Solutions, Nuance, and Conversation—as a holistic reporting strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These pillars are not necessarily present in every story but function together as a reporting strategy that can change how audiences feel about whether journalists should be delivering solutions and reduce the weight of expectation on journalists themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar: Solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions: Reporters are encouraged to seek out and rigorously report on best practices; responses to problems are newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pillar aligns with the Solutions Journalism Network's standards and practices: treat responses to social problems as legitimate news subjects and report on them with the same rigor as problem-focused reporting. In this project context the team uses both 'solutions' and the softer term 'possibilities' to moderate expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar: Nuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Nuance: Reflect a range of perspectives when covering issues; present complexity rather than simplistic or binary framings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nuance moderates expectations about what reporting can accomplish and ensures coverage represents multiple viewpoints, acknowledging journalists' limits of bias and knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar: Conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversation: Help people hear each other; position journalism as facilitator of civic dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pillar emphasizes engagement strategies and story framing that encourage civic conversation rather than merely broadcasting information. It reframes the journalist's role toward convening or facilitating community discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain investigative rigor—'both critical and constructive'
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journalism 'includes, rather than replaces, the principles of rigorous investigative reporting.' The goal is coverage that is both critical and constructive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue to provide facts and uncover problems with the same rigor as traditional investigative reporting while also elevating information that points toward potential progress or solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid prescriptive editorializing or advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journalism 'stops short of prescriptive editorializing that can veer into advocacy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain journalistic independence and avoid advocating for particular policy choices or acting as an advocate; instead, present information that enables civic decision-making and constructive dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics commitment: follow Society of Professional Journalists Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive Journalism in the South 'respects, values and seeks to abide by the Society of Professional Journalists Code of Ethics.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any constructive practice must be rooted in foundational journalistic ethics to separate journalism from other content creation and distribution forms. Treat SPJ principles as a baseline for integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-centric orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: The method, research, examples and toolkit can be used as part of initiatives to develop or redevelop sustainable, audience-centric local news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt audience research and design practices; center diverse audience perspectives when shaping coverage and product strategies to increase relevance and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center diverse audience perspectives and media-member insights
rubrics_metrics.description: This project began by researching how journalism could bring Mississippians together, starting with a diverse audience perspective along with insights from media members across the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design initiatives and reporting strategies informed by explicit audience diversity and practitioner input to ensure coverage resonates across community segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use both 'solutions' and 'possibilities' terminology to set expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: In this project context, the team uses both the term 'solutions' (connecting to SJN standards) and the term 'possibilities,' which moderates the expectation for both the reporter and the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose vocabulary that signals realistic aims: 'solutions' where rigorous evaluation exists, 'possibilities' where the intent is to explore or illuminate potential approaches without over-promising outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure digital engagement and conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: As a project approach, news outlets can test effects on measures like digital engagement metrics and conversions to subscriptions/memberships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track standard digital KPIs (pageviews, time on page, clicks, social engagement) alongside conversion events to assess whether constructive approaches drive audience actions or revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure impacts on subscriber/member growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Test effects on impacts on subscriber/member growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subscription and membership enrollment, retention, and lifetime value as metrics to evaluate whether constructive initiatives strengthen financial sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure civic engagement outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Test effects on measures of civic engagement, such as voter participation rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where feasible, correlate coverage initiatives with civic outcomes (e.g., turnout, public meeting participation), recognizing attribution challenges and using appropriate study designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure audience and community sentiment about the outlet
rubrics_metrics.description: Test effects on audience and community sentiment about a media outlet and its value to the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use surveys, focus groups, social listening, and other qualitative/quantitative tools to assess perceived trust, relevance, and community value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure recruiting metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Test effects on recruiting metrics such as internship or job applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track talent-attraction indicators to see whether constructive approaches affect the newsroom’s ability to recruit and retain staff or interns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure staff sentiment, motivation and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Test effects on staff sentiment, motivation and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess newsroom morale, perceived mission alignment, workload, and professional development outcomes as part of evaluating constructive practice adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use construct as a project approach or full brand transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: News outlets can use this model to completely transform a brand and coverage strategy, or as a project approach to test its effect on specific measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply constructive journalism either incrementally (pilot projects) or holistically (organizational transformation), and align evaluation metrics accordingly.
